Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Syed Imran Ibrahim,Praveen Kumar Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Aditya Gupta Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
Heard Sri Manish Tewari, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Praveen Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Aditya Gupta, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the material available on record.

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge sheet dated 22.7.2020 as well as summoning order dated 14.1.2021 including entire proceedings of Case No. 383 of 2021 (State of U.P. Vs. Chirag Maheshwari and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 0267 of 2019, under Section- 376, 504, 506, Indian Penal Code, Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Ghaziabad, pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 8, Ghaziabad.

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that the first information report dated 28.11.2019 has been lodged against the applicants stating therein that the first informant is an Interior Designer.

She met the applicant Chirag Maheshwari vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170678482/
1 No. 1 in a Corporate Expo, Pragati Maidan, Delhi two years prior to the incident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 21.3.2019 applicant No. 1 called the first informant for the meeting at Khan Market, Delhi and offered her a job and partnership in a business and also proposed to marry her, which was accepted by the first informant.
After that applicant No. 1 had gone to China.
On 31.3.2019 at 4.00 p.m. applicant No. 1 called first informant in J.P. Basant Continental Hotel, Basant Vihar, Delhi and made relation forcibly on the pretext of marriage.
Again on 19.4.2019 at about 2.00 p.m. applicant came at the house of the first informant and made relation with the first informant.
When the first informant forced applicant No. 1 for marriage, she came to know that applicant No. 1 is already married with applicant No. 2 namely Jyotsana Maheshwari.
When first informant decided to complain this fact to the police, applicant No. 2 is said to have extended threats to the first informant.

Thereafter, police investigated the matter and submitted the charge sheet on 22.7.2020 under Section 376 I.P.C.
against the applicant no.1 and under Section 506 I.P.C. against the applicant no.2.
Cognizance was taken by the Civil Judge (Junior Division) F.T.C., 1st, Ghaziabad on 14.01.2021 and summoned the applicants to face trial under Sections 376 and 506 I.P.C..

Learned Senior Counsel for the applicants submitted that both the parties are adults and are consenting parties and the first informant was aware of this fact that the applicant no.1 is already a married person.
It is further submitted that as per statement of the first informant recorded under Section 164, Cr.P.C., she came to know about the second marriage of the applicant no. 1 on 8.5.2019.

From the chat/messages, which were exchanged between the applicant No. 1 and first informant, it is revealed that applicant No. 1 had never made any kind of promise of marriage with the first informant as well as there is no message in the chat history with regard to marriage.
It is further submitted that there is no whisper about the date of knowledge of second marriage in the first information report.
Learned counsel for the applicants argued that the relationship between the opposite party no.2 and the applicant was consensual in nature.

Learned counsel have relied upon the decision of the Apex Court in the cases of Pramod Suryabhan Pawan Vs State of Maharashtra, AIR ONLINE 2019 SC 904, and argued that in cases where the relationship is consensual in nature, the Apex Court has quashed the proceedings and as such the present case from the evidence collected during investigation, goes to show the relationship between the two is consensual in nature and it was only after the opposite party no. 2 came to know about the first marriage of applicant, the present F.I.R.
has been lodged just in order to falsely implicate and harass them.

sentences.text: It is argued that the relationship between the opposite party no. 2 and the applicant continued from the year 2017 but the F.I.R. was lodged after about two years of the same and in the intervening period, there was no complaint whatsoever by the opposite party no. 2.
It is argued that the proceedings as initiated are totally an abuse of process of court and deserve to be quashed.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 have opposed the prayer for quashing and argued that the present case is such in which there are serious allegations against the applicant no.1.
There are allegations against the accused person and the same was on the pretext of marriage.

sentences.text: After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicants have been summoned by the trial court to face trial.
There is allegation against the applicant of committing rape upon the victim on the pretext of marriage.
The prosecutrix has supported the prosecution version in her statement recorded under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C.
From the perusal of material on record and looking into the facts of the case at this stage it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the applicants.
All the submissions made at the bar relates to the disputed question of fact, which cannot be adjudicated upon by this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

At this stage only prima facie case is to be seen in the light of the law laid down by Supreme Court in cases of R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab, A.I.R. 1960 S.C. 866, State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 426, State of Bihar Vs. P.P.Sharma, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 192 and lastly Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. Vs. Mohd. Saraful Haq and another (Para-10) 2005 SCC (Cr.)
283.

sentences.text: Great care should be taken by the High Court before embarking to scrutinise the complaint /FIR/charge-sheet in deciding whether the rarest of the rare case is made out to scuttle the prosecution in its inception and criminal proceedings should not be nipped in the bud at initial stage.
The disputed defence of the accused cannot be considered at this stage.
Moreover, the applicants have got a right of discharge and they are free to take all the submissions in the said discharge application before the trial court.

Further in the case of Priti Saraf & anr. Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & anr. : 2021 SCC Online SC 206 the Apex Court while considering the powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. relying upon the judgements rendered by the Apex Court in the cases of State of Haryana and Others Vs. Bhajan Lal and Others (1992) Suppl (1) SCC 335 and Arnab Manoranjan Goswami Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others (2021) 2 SCC 427 has held that the exercise of inherent power of the High Court is an extraordinary power which has to be exercised with great care and circumspection before embarking to scrutinise the complaint/FIR/charge-sheet in deciding whether the case is the rarest of rare case,
to scuttle the prosecution at its inception.

sentences.text: Thus, it is trite law that at the stage of quashing only the material of the prosecution has to be seen and the court cannot delve into the defence of the accused and then proceed to examine the matter on its merit by weighing the evidence so produced.

The disputed questions of facts of the case cannot be adjudged and adjudicated at this stage while exercising powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
and only the prima facie prosecution case has to be looked into and as it is.
Evidence needs to be led to substantiate the defence of the accused.
Looking to the facts of the case, the prima facie allegation against the applicants and the law as stated above, no case for interference is made out.

The present application is, accordingly,
dismissed.
